UT-2026-SB8.aiSummary: Utah SB 8 adds money for state and higher education pay in fiscal years 2026 and 2027. It funds a 2.5% pay increase for state and higher education employees, and similar funding for judicial branch and constitutional office workers, along with changes in health, dental, and retirement costs. It also sets aside money for some state employee match payments and for step and lane pay increases for employees of the Utah Schools for the Deaf and the Blind.

UT-2026-SB44.aiSummary: The bill adopts a new statewide resource management plan that replaces the earlier one. It also directs the office to monitor how federal, state, and local governments follow the plan, report any planned changes each year, and work with the commission on those changes. UT-2026-HB94.aiSummary: The law changes how people can pay or lower certain criminal debts in Utah courts. It lets a judge count approved community service toward fines, fees, surcharges, and interest at no less than $12 an hour, and it can also cut those amounts by the cost of a court-ordered treatment or class if the person finishes it and shows proof. It also changes some rules for asking to change payment plans, and it takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB52.aiSummary: This bill lets a driver license or state ID holder ask for a note that says they are a federally recognized tribal member. The Driver License Division would accept certain tribal or federal papers as proof, and the note could not name the specific tribe. UT-2026-HB220.policyArea: Attorney General, Board of Pardons and Parole, Bureau of Criminal Identification
UT-2026-HB220.aiSummary: Signed into law in Utah, this bill changes where several public safety reports are sent. It moves some reports from a legislative committee to the State Commission on Criminal and Juvenile Justice and adds new data that must go into the public safety portal, including crime in student housing, offender metrics from the Board of Pardons and Parole, prosecutorial complaint reports, and sexual assault kit reports. It also says the commission does not have to give out records it receives for the portal under the state records law.

UT-2026-HB214.policyArea: Business, Civil Procedure, Commerce and Trade
UT-2026-HB214.aiSummary: The law changes Utah rules on lawsuits over firearms and firearm-related items. It says a claim against a gun maker, seller, or trade group must fit certain listed exceptions and must give specific facts, and courts must dismiss claims that do not meet those rules. It also lets a winning defendant get attorney fees and court costs, bars foreign nations from using those exceptions, and stops local governments from imposing civil liability in this area. It takes effect on May 6, 2026.

UT-2026-HB385.aiSummary: This law creates a state license for people who sell certain specialized products, like some tobacco, nicotine, kratom, and cannabinoid items, and sets yearly fees for the license. UT-2026-HB337.policyArea: Cigarette and Tobacco Taxes, Health and Human Services, Revenue and Taxation
UT-2026-HB337.aiSummary: Governor signed this measure, and most changes take effect July 1, 2026. It raises Utah taxes on cigarettes, e-cigarettes, and nontherapeutic nicotine devices, and changes the tax on some other nicotine products to a per-item tax or a price-based tax depending on the product type. It also adds a one-time inventory tax on cigarettes already in stock when the higher tax starts, and sends the extra revenue from the newer nicotine product taxes to the General Fund.
